instructions.cross_packet_rule: Use cross_packet_terms for likely synonyms, owners, consumers, and seams outside this packet.
instructions.family_key_rule: Every assigned raw family key must have exactly one family_key_assignments row and at least one mapped feature.
instructions.objective: Normalize every assigned validated audit atom into an exhaustive local inventory of distinct Puppet Master features, systems, tools, workflows, GUI surfaces, integrations, data models, governance controls, or cross-cutting concerns. Preserve under-specification, contradictions, unknowns, and explicit non-gaps.
instructions.output_rule: Write exactly one strict-schema JSON payload in the assigned output directory and then return PMR1.
instructions.partition_rule: Every atom_id must appear in exactly one feature.atom_ids array; no omission or duplication.
instructions.research_rule: Do not browse in this phase. Give every normalized feature at least one concrete external-research question for the mandatory next phase; do not treat absence of seed queries as permission to omit research.
instructions.scenario_rule: Give every feature at least one falsifiable scenario requirement for later certification.
instructions.split_merge_rule: Split concepts with distinct lifecycle, authority, consumers, or failure semantics. Merge only true synonyms describing the same product concept; record aliases and relationships instead of collapsing uncertainty.

atoms.statement: RSC-004 names current and retired names, JSON/JSONC, management modes, dry-run, and rollback, but its acceptance list does not specify precedence, parser dialect, unknown-key preservation, malformed-input handling, atomic writes, locking, idempotency, backup identity, dry-run equivalence, or rollback-result oracles.
atoms.title: Config migration fixtures omit critical edge-state semantics

atoms.statement: RSC-005 establishes read-only, no-shell, no-write defaults for agentic issue and pull-request triage and requires explicit escalation receipts before access to sensitive tools or release capabilities.
atoms.title: Agentic CI starts with least authority

atoms.statement: The taint requirement does not define an envelope schema, source identity, transitive propagation through derived data and caches, permitted uses, declassification authority, mixed-trust joins, retention/redaction, refusal and recovery states, audit events, or adversarial falsification fixtures.
atoms.title: AI-CI taint has no executable propagation contract

atoms.statement: RSC-005 lists only the release document as an implementation surface even though its target-doc list names GitHub integration, permissions, decision policy, contracts, automated testing, and governance; it does not assign which owner enforces taint, escalation, cache/OIDC validation, publish denial, or receipt consumption.
atoms.title: AI-CI enforcement ownership is not propagated

atoms.statement: RSC-006 requires packaged components to declare platform security and linking state, classifies startup failures, and tests macOS, Windows, and Linux platform-specific conditions.
atoms.title: Platform launch failures have distinct diagnostic classes

atoms.statement: RSC-006 does not enumerate supported OS versions and architectures, artifact-to-matrix coverage, library and entitlement expectations, diagnostic codes and remediation, recovery/retry behavior, performance thresholds, offline distinctions, accessibility/localization requirements, or the GUI owner's obligation to present the classified state truthfully.
atoms.title: Platform compatibility matrix lacks coverage and recovery semantics

atoms.statement: RSC-007 requires install validation to fail on package ownership or mode mismatches, records source/hash/channel/rollback for self-update, and surfaces signing, notarization, and entitlement checks before rollout.
atoms.title: Install and update flows produce provenance receipts

atoms.statement: RSC-007 does not define update states, authorization and process-lock boundaries, download verification order, channel transition rules, rollout pause/cancel behavior, retry/idempotency, partial-install recovery, offline handling, migration coupling, rollback eligibility, or the user-visible truth for each failure state.
atoms.title: Install and update lifecycle is not specified

atoms.statement: RSC-008 defines minimum ReleaseArtifactReceipt, SBOM receipt, UpdateMetadata, and MigrationReceipt fields and requires install/update validation to fail closed on missing or stale critical evidence.
atoms.title: Signing, SBOM, update, and migration receipts fail closed

atoms.statement: RSC-008 requires user-visible update failure state metadata but classifies itself as not GUI-related and does not bind failure_state_copy_ref to a GUI owner or define presentation, action, accessibility, localization, or stale-state prevention requirements.
atoms.title: User-visible update failure state conflicts with GUI classification

atoms.statement: RSC-008 enumerates receipt fields but does not define concrete schemas, identifiers and referential-integrity rules, the meaning of question-mark optionality, freshness windows, trusted clocks, verifier-result enum, accepted algorithms/formats, key rotation/revocation, receipt signing, evidence access/retention/redaction, size and component-count limits, or recovery behavior for stale or partially verified receipts.
atoms.title: Receipt field lists lack executable semantics and lifecycle rules

cross_document_questions: Which named owner document defines and enforces the AI-CI taint envelope, escalation receipt, cache provenance, OIDC provenance, and publish-denial contracts consumed by release workflows?
Which GUI owner consumes update failure_state_copy_ref and platform diagnostic classes, and what contract prevents stale or misleading user-visible release state?
Where are supported OS, architecture, library, entitlement, sandbox, GPU, and network matrix identities canonically enumerated for RSC-006?
Which storage and FileSafe contracts own migration backup identity, retention, encryption, atomic restoration, and destructive-action authorization?
Which artifact/schema owner materializes and validates ReleaseArtifactReceipt, SBOM receipt, UpdateMetadata, and MigrationReceipt referential integrity?

atoms.statement: Run Graph is explicitly defined as the canonical graph and lineage inspection projection over runtime nodes and graph generations, rather than a tier authority.
atoms.title: Canonical Run Graph scope is explicit

atoms.statement: Host access pivots disclose confidence and health but do not define an executable validation and failure contract for untrusted dynamic URLs, schemes, origins, permission denial, or offline targets.
atoms.title: Host access pivots lack target-safety semantics

atoms.statement: Active runtime identity and user-selected run focus are explicitly separate, with live and historical modes constrained by their relationship.
atoms.title: Active and focused run truth are separated

atoms.statement: The shared destination concept enumerates callers and desired fidelity but does not define the payload fields, required-by-object rules, versioning, conflict precedence, or invalid-target result semantics.
atoms.title: Shared deep-link payload is not field-complete

atoms.statement: The graph names scaling techniques but supplies no node/edge thresholds, frame or interaction budgets, memory bounds, update-lag limits, degradation order, or measurable large-graph fixture.
atoms.title: Large-graph behavior has no quantitative bounds

atoms.statement: The inspector defines a rich disclosure set but no field-level permission, redaction, privacy-lifecycle, localization, or accessibility contract for sensitive and unavailable values.
atoms.title: Inspector disclosure policy is unspecified

atoms.statement: Runtime join authority is explicitly migrated from tier identity to node, attempt, blocked episode, generation, lane, artifact, and provider-platform scopes.
atoms.title: Runtime identity modernization is explicit

atoms.statement: The active tab model and blocked-action identity replace tier-era navigation and request identifiers, with legacy tokens constrained to compatibility lineage.
atoms.title: Tier and HITL compatibility authority is bounded

atoms.statement: Projection-trust disclosure and gating are mandatory, but trust-state enums, transition triggers, per-action gate outcomes, recovery rules, and observable error codes are not specified here.
atoms.title: Projection-trust gating is not executable

atoms.statement: The unit correctly refuses non-local authority but explicitly leaves several prerequisite owner contracts outside this document, without a consumed version, readiness condition, or compatibility behavior.
atoms.title: Adjacent owner contracts remain unresolved

atoms.statement: Validation targets are named, but most are manual reviews or plan-governance scripts; no executable fixture matrix defines inputs, expected routes, trust states, disabled reasons, and failure outputs.
atoms.title: Validation lacks behavioral acceptance oracles

atoms.statement: Historical focus persistence is detailed, but revision ownership, atomic update semantics, concurrent-writer resolution, invalid restored selections, and offline revalidation are left open.
atoms.title: Historical focus persistence lacks conflict semantics

atoms.statement: GoalRun, WorkGraph, verification, and plan-preparation overlays have an explicit projection-only authority boundary against their runtime and compiler owners.
atoms.title: WorkGraph overlay authority is bounded

atoms.statement: The execution projection aggregates many independently updating records but does not define correlation keys, ordering, snapshot consistency, source precedence, partial-availability semantics, or reconciliation after contradictory updates.
atoms.title: Execution progress has no consistency model

atoms.statement: RGV-014 is owned by Run_Graph_View.md yet canonically specifies the Orchestrator Plan Compile tab, while RGV-013 says Run Graph does not replace Plan Compile scope; the consumption and ownership boundary is unresolved.
atoms.title: Plan Compile projection is placed under conflicting ownership

atoms.statement: UsageRecord identity and anti-double-counting requirements are strong, but the allowed degraded fallback lacks a deterministic priority, ambiguity rule, disabled reason, user disclosure, and recovery path.
atoms.title: Degraded usage routing is ambiguous
